decisions.rationale: Valid: the await continuation was described as a task, against the event-loop page's microtask model. The event-loop item is now html-css-js-final-mcq-22, and its key feedback at line 180 reads 'resumes as a microtask on the single main thread'; 'resumes as a task' appears nowhere in the bank.

Valid: the 25% track distractor was untaught, and the item could be answered by elimination. In html-css-js-final-mcq-03, lines 22-25 now offer repeat(4, 225px), repeat(auto-fill, 225px), repeat(4, 1fr) and 4fr; each is settled by gap arithmetic or fr, and '25%' is absent. Residual, not blocking: the grid page still says only that fr shares 'the leftover space after fixed tracks'. It does not state the gap interaction that the key feedback at line 24 uses, although it follows from the taught fact that gaps take space and the other three options are eliminated by it.

Valid: the dialog distractor was rejected by an untaught 'expected pattern', while the accessibility page's 'Tab out of every part' made it appealable. Line 185's feedback now cites the page's own trap definition (focus that Tab, Shift+Tab or Escape cannot move out), which is the finding's named fallback remedy, and 'expected pattern' is gone. Residual: the page sentence 'you must be able to Tab out of every part' remains. The finding marked that rewording optional, and it belongs to the module branch.

Valid: the feedback said 'request' where 'response' was meant. The fetch(...).json() item has been removed, and 'request is read' does not occur in the bank; position 26 is now the promise-chain trace at lines 211-219.

Valid: a Network-panel 200 for a CORS-blocked call contradicts the CORS page's 'CORS error' row. That item has been removed ('server answered' is absent), and the CORS/proxy slot is now html-css-js-final-mcq-29 (lines 239-243): a static-server 404 because server.proxy is dev-only, which matches the CORS page.

Valid: the old item 01 re-keyed the debugging quiz's Step into outcome. html-css-js-final-mcq-01 (lines 5-11) is now an off-by-one loop bound found while stepping, a TypeError on items[3]. 'Step into' is absent from the bank, and no off-by-one decision appears in the debugging artifact.gift or the dom-tooling practice.gift.

Valid: the old cookie item re-keyed 'script reads localStorage, not the HttpOnly cookie', which is practised three times. html-css-js-final-mcq-12 (lines 94-98) is now a diagnosis of a Secure cookie on plain-HTTP staging with page and API on one origin. The cookies page teaches 'Secure sends it over HTTPS only', and the reused 'other way round' distractor is gone.

Valid: the heading-skip item merged two semantic-quiz items. html-css-js-final-mcq-02 (lines 14-18) now keys footer closing an article. The page defines footer as closing information 'for the page or its section' but practises it only at page level, and no h4 or heading-skip item remains.

Valid: the old item 16 was Course Review Activity 2 with border-box applied (368/396 px). Neither 368 nor 396 appears in the bank. Box-model arithmetic is now only item 04 (lines 28-32, margin collapse), and html-css-js-final-mcq-15 (lines 116-121) is a new-context mobile-first fix for an unshrinkable flex row.

Valid: the old item merged practised typeof/isArray/const facts. typeof and Array.isArray are absent. html-css-js-final-mcq-19 (lines 148-155) ports Java int division (7 / 2) used as a loop bound, which builds on the page's 'one Number type, no int' without re-asking an activity. A Node 24.2 run prints 3.5, 1, 2, 3, matching the key at line 155.

Valid: the old three-case error item re-asked the http-errors activities and Course Review A3, with key-shaped options. That item is gone ('res.ok and the content-type' is absent). Error handling is now keyed by item 11 (lines 87-91, server-only rule) and item 25 (lines 199-208, a caller ignoring save's { ok: false } result), which applies the page's result-object pattern rather than repeating it.

Valid: the old CORS item copied page Activity 1 and quiz o3, and its stem cued the key. html-css-js-final-mcq-29 (lines 239-243) is an applied production diagnosis (a static server answers 404 for /api because server.proxy is dev-only); the stem states no requirement and 'no-cors' is absent.

Valid: the old item was the fetching-data 'Why is it undefined?' activity (missing await on res.json()). res.json does not appear in the bank. Position 26 is now a promise-chain trace (lines 211-219), and the fetch slot at item 25 (lines 199-208) is a different bug.

Valid: in the BigInt/== item every option shared the fix prefix, and the item re-keyed practised facts. 'BigInt' and '1n' are absent from the bank. html-css-js-final-mcq-06 (lines 44-51), a const object mutated through a reassigned parameter, has four distinct outcomes.

Valid: the let/const fill-in re-asked let-const Activity 2 and shared item 17's key. No fill-in remains, and the const-binding decision is keyed only once, by item 06 (lines 44-51). The freed slot went to promises (item 26, lines 211-219), as recommended.

Valid: band-1 items sat late and band-3 items sat early. The current order puts the async/fetch multi-step items at 21-30, including the timing and shallow-spread items 27 (lines 222-229) and 28 (lines 232-236). No recall-only item remains in the final third. Residual dips, not blocking: the box-model calculation at item 04 (lines 28-32) and the flex-shrink calculation at item 08 (lines 64-70, now with equal bases) precede the lighter items 10 and 11 (lines 80-91). The order is broadly easier to harder.

Valid: shallow spread was keyed twice, and promises had no then-chain key. Shallow spread is now keyed once, by item 28 (line 234). Promises gets its own multi-step chain trace in item 26 (lines 211-219), combining value passing with a conditional throw, which goes beyond the quiz's abstract 'thrown in then'. Node 24.2 prints 'B too big 6', matching line 216.

Valid: same root cause as hcj-gift-sme-01, plus a distractor that named a function call the stem did not show. In item 22, the key feedback at line 180 says 'resumes as a microtask', and the first distractor at line 177 refers to 'one more await just before the loop', which matches the stem at line 176.

Valid: the stem's log answered two distractors and the key repeated the stem. The log at line 183 is now neutral: a div with tabindex="0" that Tab focuses, and an a element with an href holding only an icon with aria-label="Help". The key at line 184 interprets the symptom rather than restating it.
Valid: 'fixes that status' is ambiguous for non-native readers. Item 11 at line 87 now reads 'the API is specified to answer 400 for it', and the item sits in the first half.

Valid: a then after catch relied on untaught catch-returns-a-promise behaviour. html-css-js-final-mcq-26 now ends the chain at catch (line 215), so no option depends on it. Node 24.2 prints 'B too big 6', matching the key at line 216.
Valid: an a element without an href would itself be a keyboard barrier. Line 183 now reads 'an a element with an href, holding only an icon, with aria-label="Help"; Tab reaches it'.

Valid: the BigInt key did not say the id must never pass through Number. The BigInt item has been removed ('BigInt' is absent), and position 19 (lines 148-155) is the 7 / 2 port, verified in Node 24.2.

Valid: the revised grid distractors (300px, 3 columns) no longer tested gap or fr. Lines 22-25 now hold repeat(4, 225px) (overflows by the gaps), repeat(auto-fill, 225px) (fits three), the key repeat(4, 1fr) and 4fr (one track), and each one turns on the gap or on fr.

Valid: the comparison item had filler distractors and re-asked let-const Activity 4. It has been replaced by html-css-js-final-mcq-06 (lines 44-51), whose three distractors are real misconceptions: reassigning the parameter reaches the caller (line 48), the parameter reassignment reassigns the const (line 49), and const forbids mutation (line 50).

Valid: the POST had no Content-Type, which the course teaches yields 415, not 400. Line 201 now sends headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" }, so the ignored result object (key at line 206) is the only defect.

Valid: the stem did not place the API, so the SameSite=Strict distractor was defensible. Line 94 now says 'Staging serves the page and the API together at http://staging.example.com', which settles line 96 as same-site. The key feedback at line 98 adds that browsers do not keep a Secure cookie that arrives over HTTP.

Valid: same defect as hcj-gift-sme-l2-01, a stem 400 that conflicted with the taught 415 for an untyped string body. Line 201 now sets Content-Type to application/json, so the stem's 400 (line 199) matches what the course teaches.

Valid: undeclared status resolves to window.status in a browser. Line 246 now declares 'button is that button and note is a status paragraph', and lines 247 and 249 use note.textContent; 'window.status' and a bare status identifier are absent from item 30.

Valid: the distractor referred to 'the loop', which the stem did not show, and the stem itself refuted it. Line 253 is now 'Only Working..., because the browser paints the first change in a task and skips later ones', a real rendering misconception, and its feedback teaches the render-after-task rule. 'loop stops the last line' is absent.
